notes: Also known as: Glossy abelia. Compact shrub with glossy leaves and tubular white-pink flowers; long bloom season.
Also known as: Lady's finger, Gumbo. Warm-season fruiting vegetable in the Malvaceae family with edible pods, also known as lady's finger, heat-loving.
Evergreen conifer with soft, flat needles and upright cones that disintegrate on the tree. Most popular Christmas tree genus alongside spruce.
Graceful maple with delicate lobed leaves; red, green, or variegated; stunning fall color.
Deciduous trees in the Sapindaceae family known for brilliant fall foliage, many species are popular landscape trees.
Also known as: Kiwifruit. Vining fruit in the Actinidiaceae family with fuzzy brown fruit and green flesh, requires male and female plants.
Also known as: Tree of Life. Massive African tree with a hugely swollen trunk that stores water, sparse crown, and edible fruit rich in vitamin C.
Delicate ferns in the Adiantum genus with fan-shaped leaflets, requiring high humidity and consistent moisture.
Also known as: Silver vase plant. Bromeliads with pink flower spikes and silver-banded leaves.
Spherical green algae colony that grows naturally in cold, clear lakes. A popular low-maintenance aquatic novelty plant.
Also known as: Tree houseleek. Succulents in the Crassulaceae family with rosette-forming leaves, some varieties are monocarpic.
Also known as: Lipstick vine. Trailing gesneriad with tubular red flowers emerging from dark calyxes like lipstick.

Also known as: Conker tree, Buckeye. Large deciduous trees in the Sapindaceae family with palmate leaves, showy white or red flower candles in late spring, and spiny husks holding glossy brown conkers; not the edible sweet chestnut (Castanea).
Also known as: African lily. Clump-forming perennial with strap-shaped leaves and spectacular rounded clusters of blue, purple, or white trumpet flowers on tall stalks.
Also known as: Hyssop. Aromatic perennial with dense spikes of tubular flowers in orange, pink, purple, or blue; a magnet for hummingbirds, bees, and butterflies.

Rosette-forming succulent with thick, fleshy leaves often tipped with spines. Extremely drought tolerant. Many species are monocarpic — they bloom once after many years and then die, but produce offsets (pups).
Highly fragrant summer bulb. White tubular flowers. Tender—lift before frost. Used in perfumery.
Tropical agave cultivated for its hard, strong leaf fibers used in rope, twine, carpet, and composite materials. Each plant produces 200-250 usable leaves over its lifetime.
Also known as: Floss flower. Compact bedding annual in the Asteraceae family with fluffy, powder-puff clusters of blue, lavender, pink, or white flowers from early summer to frost.
Aglaonema cultivar with pink-splashed variegation on green leaves; bright indirect light enhances color.
Striking Aglaonema cultivar with deep pink or red variegation on dark green leaves, low-light tolerant like other Chinese evergreens.
Colorful Aglaonema cultivar with striking pink, cream, and green variegation on compact foliage; one of the most colorful Chinese evergreen varieties.
Also known as: Chinese evergreen. Low-light tolerant aroids with variegated foliage in shades of green, silver, pink, or red.
Also known as: Bugleweed. Low groundcover with blue flower spikes and bronze or green foliage; spreads by runners.

Also known as: Mimosa tree, Persian silk tree. Fast-growing, umbrella-shaped deciduous tree in the Fabaceae family with fern-like leaves that fold at night and fluffy pink powder-puff flowers in summer; invasive in parts of the southeastern United States.
Ornamental flowering bulbs in the Amaryllidaceae family, include edible onions and ornamental varieties.
Mild-flavored allium with a long white shaft and fan of flat green leaves. A staple in European cooking, especially French cuisine (vichyssoise, leek and potato soup).
Mild, sweet-flavored member of the Allium family that forms clusters of small, elongated bulbs prized in French and Asian cuisine for their delicate flavor.
Allium with mild edible green tops and white bases, used fresh in many cuisines.
Essential culinary bulb in the Allium family, planted in fall and harvested the following summer; hardneck types produce flavorful scapes, softneck types store longer.
Also known as: Nira. Perennial herbs in the Amaryllidaceae family with flat leaves and garlic flavor, essential in Chinese cuisine.
Compact Alocasia with extraordinarily textured, thick leaves featuring deep silvery-green coloring and prominent dark veining that resembles dragon scales.
Compact Alocasia cultivar from Borneo with rigid, silvery-green leaves featuring deeply etched dark green veins and a textured, almost metallic surface.
Also known as: Mirror plant, Red copper. Alocasia with metallic copper-bronze leaves and pronounced veins; compact, jewel-like foliage.
Alocasia with unique leaf shape—elongated "tail" like a stingray; large foliage plant.
Also known as: Grey dragon. Compact gray-green Alocasia with textured, velvety leaves; dwarf elephant ear.
Also known as: Green velvet. Velvety green Alocasia with prominent white veins; similar to Black Velvet but green. Requires high humidity.
Compact Alocasia with velvety black leaves and silver veins; dramatic foliage plant requiring high humidity.
Alocasia with striped zebra-pattern stems and arrow-shaped leaves; striking tropical aroid.

Also known as: African mask plant. Dramatic aroid with arrow-shaped, dark green leaves featuring bold white or silver veining. Parent hybrid of the smaller Alocasia Polly. Despite the name, it is a hybrid, not from the Amazon.
Also known as: African mask. Compact hybrid Alocasia with arrow-shaped, dark green leaves and white veins; popular cultivar.
Compact aloe with dark green to black-tinted leaves; same care as aloe vera. Toxic to pets.
Also known as: Lemon beebrush, Cedrón. Deciduous shrubby herb in the Verbenaceae family with narrow leaves that release the most intense lemon scent of any herb; used for tea, desserts, and syrups.

Also known as: Peruvian lily, Lily of the Incas. Tuberous perennials in the Alstroemeriaceae family with azalea-like, speckled flowers in every color but blue on 30-100 cm stems from early summer to frost; one of the longest-lasting cut flowers.
Pseudo-cereal in the Amaranthaceae family. Gluten-free grain; seeds high in protein. Drought tolerant. Ancient crop of the Americas.
Also known as: Chinese spinach. Heat-tolerant leafy green and grain crop in the Amaranthaceae family; nutritious leaves and edible seeds, thrives in summer heat.
Also known as: Juneberry. Small tree or large shrub with white spring flowers, edible berries, and brilliant fall color.
Native prairie shrub with silvery-gray foliage and purple flower spikes; nitrogen-fixing, drought tolerant, attracts pollinators.
World's largest unbranched flower structure, producing a massive spathe that smells of rotting flesh when blooming. Blooms are rare, occurring every 7-10 years.
Tropical evergreen tree in the Anacardiaceae family producing kidney-shaped nuts attached to fleshy cashew apples. Native to Brazil, now grown across the tropics.
Tropical bromeliad in the Bromeliaceae family producing sweet aggregate fruits from the crown.
Tall native prairie grass with blue-green stems that turn reddish in fall; three-forked seed heads.
Also known as: Poppy anemone. Spring-blooming tuberous perennials. Anemone blanda (early) and A. coronaria (poppy). Plant in fall; dormant after flowering.
Annual herbs in the Apiaceae family with feathery leaves and seeds, both leaves and seeds are used.
Also known as: Summer snapdragon. Upright spikes of snapdragon-like flowers in purple, pink, or white; heat-tolerant and low-maintenance.

Also known as: Custard apple, Chirimoya. Subtropical fruit tree in the Annonaceae family bearing heart-shaped green fruits with creamy white flesh that tastes like banana, pineapple, and vanilla custard; related to atemoya, sugar apple, and soursop.
Tropical aroids with colorful spathes and glossy foliage, long-lasting blooms.
Anthurium with velvety heart-shaped leaves and prominent white veins; grown for foliage, not flowers.
Velvet-leaved aroid with large, heart-shaped, dark green leaves featuring prominent crystalline silver venation. One of the most popular ornamental anthuriums for collectors.
Rosette-forming anthurium with large, wavy, leathery leaves that form a bird's nest shape. Unlike typical anthuriums, grown for dramatic foliage rather than colorful spathes.
Large velvety Anthurium with dark green leaves and prominent pale veins; dramatic foliage plant native to Colombia.
Also known as: King Anthurium. Prized collector aroid with spectacularly long, corrugated, pendant leaves that can reach over 1 meter. The deeply rippled texture is unmistakable.
Anthurium with long, narrow strap-like leaves; unique form among anthuriums.
Majestic collector aroid with elongated, dark velvety leaves up to 1.8m long featuring silvery-white veining. One of the most prized Anthurium species.
Hardy, low-light aquarium plant with thick dark green leaves that grows attached to rocks and driftwood.
Stalk vegetables in the Apiaceae family, require consistent moisture and rich soil, challenging to grow.
Celery root in the Apiaceae family, grown for its edible swollen stem base with celery-like flavor, popular in European cuisine.
Floating aquatic with fragrant white flowers. Aponogeton blooms spring and fall. Submerged planting; leaves float.
Trailing cactus with long, thin stems covered in spines, produces bright pink or red flowers.
Also known as: Broadleaf Amazon Sword, Paniculatus Sword. Popular background aquarium plant with large, bright-green rosette leaves that can grow up to 50 cm tall.

Also known as: Granny's Bonnet. Delicate woodland perennial with distinctive spurred flowers in vivid color combinations—red & yellow, blue & white, pink & purple. Blooms mid-spring to early summer; attracts hummingbirds. Short-lived (3-4 years) but self-seeds freely to naturalize.
Annual legume in the Fabaceae family. Nuts develop underground (geocarpy). Valencia, Spanish, Virginia types. Warm-season; needs sandy soil.
Also known as: Chilean Pine, Chile Pine. Ancient evergreen conifer with distinctive spiny, overlapping leaves and a striking symmetrical silhouette.
Perennial root in the Brassicaceae family with pungent, spicy roots used for condiments, can spread aggressively.

The world's largest tree-borne fruit, with individual fruits weighing up to 35 kg. A tropical evergreen producing sweet, aromatic golden flesh used fresh, dried, or as a popular meat substitute when young and unripe.
Monarch host plant with pink flowers; prefers moist to wet soil; native to wetlands.
Essential Monarch butterfly host plant; fragrant pink flowers; spreads by rhizomes; full sun.
Native milkweed with bright orange flowers; essential for monarch butterflies.
Native North American tree in the Annonaceae family with custard-like tropical-flavored fruits.
Also known as: Garden asparagus. Perennial vegetable with tender edible spears, takes 2-3 years to establish.
Also known as: Lace fern, Plumosa fern. Not a true fern—lacey foliage plant in Asparagaceae; feathery stems. Berries and sap toxic to pets.
Variegated form of the cast iron plant with cream or white stripes on narrow leaves; equally indestructible and low-light tolerant.
Epiphytic fern with wavy, strap-like fronds emerging from a central rosette, resembles a bird's nest.
Compact alpine aster with daisy-like flowers in late spring to summer. Cold hardy, suited to rock gardens and alpine troughs.
Also known as: False spirea. Feathery plumes in pink, white, or red; thrives in moist shade.
Small, round cactus with star-shaped pattern, very slow-growing and rare.
Hardy deciduous fern with silvery-gray fronds brushed with purple and burgundy along the midribs; one of the most colorful ferns for shaded gardens.
Mat-forming alpine perennial in the Brassicaceae family with masses of spring flowers, excellent for rock gardens.
Annual grass in the Poaceae family. Cereal for oatmeal, feed, and hay. Cool-season; tolerates wetter soils than wheat. Spring and winter types.
Also known as: Carambola, Star Apple, Five-Corner Fruit. Tropical fruit tree producing distinctive star-shaped cross-section fruits with a sweet-tart flavor.
Evergreen tree native to the Indian subcontinent, widely cultivated for its medicinal and insecticidal properties. Nearly every part of the tree has been used in traditional medicine.
Fast-growing grasses in the Poaceae family, can be clumping or running types, popular for screening and containers. Not related to lucky bamboo, which is a Dracaena.
Also known as: Wild indigo. Native legume with blue flowers and blue-gray foliage; nitrogen-fixing; drought tolerant.
Heat-loving vining herb in the Basellaceae family; succulent leaves and stems. Thrives in summer when true spinach bolts.
Cane begonias with wing-shaped spotted leaves and pendent flower clusters in red, pink, or white.
Dramatic rhizomatous begonia with dark, textured leaves covered in cone-shaped black spikes (bullae). One of the most unusual-looking houseplants available. Native to limestone caves in Vietnam.
Cane begonia with silver-spotted leaves, red undersides, and white flower clusters. The most commonly sold form is the 'Wightii' cultivar.
Rhizomatous begonia grown for its spectacular, multicolored foliage in swirling patterns of silver, purple, pink, red, and green. One of the most ornamental houseplant species.
Annual and perennial flowers in the Begoniaceae family with colorful blooms and attractive foliage, shade-tolerant.
Flowering begonias grown from tubers, often with large showy blooms in various colors.
Also known as: Wax gourd. Large gourd in the Cucurbitaceae family with waxy coating, mild flavor, popular in Asian soups and stir-fries.
Thorny shrub with red, gold, or green foliage; small berries; invasive in many regions.

Also known as: Curry tree, Kadi patta, Sweet neem. Small aromatic tree in the Rutaceae family whose glossy pinnate leaves are fried in oil at the start of countless South Indian and Sri Lankan dishes; unrelated to the silver-leaved curry plant (Helichrysum) or to curry powder.
Also known as: Rainbow chard. Leafy green vegetable in the Amaranthaceae family with colorful stems, can be harvested continuously throughout season.
Also known as: Garden beet, Red beet. Root vegetables in the Amaranthaceae family, both roots and greens are edible, prefer cool weather.
Multi-trunk birch with distinctive peeling cinnamon-brown bark; tolerates wet soils.
Deciduous trees in the Betulaceae family with distinctive white or colored bark, prefer cool climates and moist soil.
Evergreen to semi-evergreen vine with orange-red trumpet flowers in spring; hummingbird magnet.
Silver Lady Fern with upright fronds forming a trunk-like base. Tolerates slightly drier air than many ferns.
Evergreen hardy fern of cool, moist woodlands with dimorphic fronds: sterile fronds spread outward while narrow fertile fronds grow upright from the center. Excellent for shaded, acidic garden beds.
Also known as: Starflower. Annual herb in the Boraginaceae family with edible blue flowers and cucumber-flavored leaves. Used in salads, drinks, and as a companion plant for tomatoes and squash.
Vigorous tropical vine with brilliant papery bracts in magenta, purple, red, orange, white, or pink that surround tiny true flowers, thriving in hot, dry climates.
Native prairie grass with oat-like flowers arranged along one side of the stem; state grass of Texas.
Low native prairie grass with distinctive horizontal flower spikes resembling eyelashes; drought tolerant.
Leafy green vegetables in the Brassicaceae family with peppery flavor, fast-growing and cold-hardy.
Also known as: Rapeseed. Oilseed crop in the Brassicaceae family. Low-erucic-acid rapeseed for edible oil and biodiesel. Yellow flowers. Spring and winter types.
Also known as: Swede, Neep. Root vegetables in the Brassicaceae family, cross between turnip and cabbage, prefer cool weather.

Also known as: Nagoya ornamental kale. Cool-season annual grown for its striking rosettes of ruffled or fringed leaves in purple, pink, white, and cream; color intensifies as temperatures drop below 55°F (13°C).
Cold-hardy leafy green in the Brassicaceae family, flavor improves after frost, can overwinter in mild climates.
Also known as: Chinese broccoli, Kai-lan, Chinese kale. Chinese broccoli in the Brassicaceae family with thick stems and small flower heads, essential in Chinese cuisine.
Cruciferous vegetables in the Brassicaceae family, form white, purple, or orange heads, prefer cool weather.
Leafy vegetables in the Brassicaceae family, form tight heads, prefer cool weather.
Cruciferous vegetables in the Brassicaceae family, produce small cabbage-like sprouts along stem, flavor improves after frost.
Unique vegetables in the Brassicaceae family with swollen stem base, both bulb and leaves are edible, fast-growing.
Cruciferous vegetables in the Brassicaceae family, harvest central head and side shoots, prefer cool weather.
Also known as: Collards. Leafy green vegetable in the Brassicaceae family, cold-hardy and can overwinter in mild climates.
Mild, slightly peppery. Harvest at first true leaves (8–12 days).
Also known as: Pak choi. Leafy green vegetable in the Brassicaceae family, fast-growing and mild-flavored, popular in Chinese cuisine.
Also known as: Chinese cabbage, Wombok, Pe-tsai. Chinese cabbage in the Brassicaceae family with elongated, barrel-shaped heads, essential in Chinese cuisine.
Also known as: White turnip. Root vegetables in the Brassicaceae family, both roots and greens are edible, prefer cool weather.
Japanese mustard green in the Brassicaceae family; feathery, serrated leaves with mild peppery flavor. Popular in salads and stir-fries.
Also known as: Chinese flowering cabbage. Leafy green vegetables in the Brassicaceae family, popular in Chinese cuisine with tender stems and small yellow flowers.
Edible leaves of the turnip root; nutritious, slightly peppery. Harvest before or alongside roots; flavor improves after light frost.
Asian green in the Brassicaceae family; dark green spoon-shaped leaves in a flat rosette. Mild, mustard-like flavor; cold-hardy.
Mild mustard-like microgreens from broccoli raab. Harvest at first true leaves (8–12 days).

Young seedlings harvested within 1-3 weeks of germination. Sprouts are grown in water only; microgreens are grown on a thin layer of soil or growing medium. Nutrient-dense and easy to grow indoors year-round. Popular mixes combine varied flavors, colors, and textures.
Also known as: Summer lilac. Arching shrub with fragrant flower spikes; attracts butterflies; can be invasive.
Evergreen plants that tolerate cold winter temperatures, provide year-round structure and color in landscapes.
Evergreen shrubs in the Buxaceae family with dense foliage, popular for hedges and topiary, slow-growing and long-lived.
Also known as: Red gram, Gandules. Drought-hardy tropical legume widely grown in South Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean for its protein-rich seeds used in dal, soups, and stews.
Also known as: Angel wings, Heart of Jesus. Tuberous aroid with arrow-shaped leaves in pink, red, white, or green; grown for foliage, goes dormant in winter.
Plants in Marantaceae family with leaves that fold up at night (nyctinasty), require high humidity.
Miniature petunia-like flowers in many colors; prolific bloomer for containers and hanging baskets.
Deciduous shrub with arching branches and vivid magenta-purple berry clusters that encircle the stems in autumn, providing striking fall and winter interest.

Also known as: Scotch heather, Ling. Low evergreen shrub in the Ericaceae family forming mounds of tiny scale-like leaves, covered in late summer and autumn with spikes of pink, purple, or white bell flowers; foliage of many cultivars turns gold or red in winter.

Also known as: Common camas, Small camas. Native North American bulb producing tall spikes of starry blue, purple, or white flowers in late spring—historically an important food source for Indigenous peoples.
Evergreen shrub whose leaves produce black, green, oolong, and white tea.
Low-growing alpine bellflowers with blue or purple bells. Cold hardy, suited to rock gardens and crevices.
Also known as: Bellflower, Garden campanula. Classic cottage garden biennials and perennials with bell-shaped flowers in blue, purple, pink, and white. Distinct from the alpine campanula species.
Also known as: Trumpet creeper. Vigorous vine with orange-red trumpet flowers; very fast-growing, can be invasive.
Also known as: Sweet pepper. Sweet peppers in the Solanaceae family with blocky, thick-walled fruits, most popular pepper variety.
Mild Mexican chile pepper with wide, dark green, heart-shaped fruits that are essential in chiles rellenos, mole sauces, and when dried become the smoky-sweet ancho chile.
Medium-hot pepper (10,000-23,000 Scoville) commonly used in Mexican cuisine, especially salsas and pico de gallo. Smaller and hotter than jalapeños.
Very hot peppers in the Solanaceae family, among the hottest common peppers, use with extreme caution.
Tropical herbaceous tree in the Caricaceae family with orange-fleshed fruits, fast-growing.
Also known as: Giant cactus. Iconic columnar cactus of the Sonoran Desert, growing up to 12m tall with arm-like branches. Extremely slow-growing; takes 10 years to reach 2.5cm.
Hardy deciduous tree with fluted bark; excellent for hedging and topiary.
Annual oilseed in the Asteraceae family. High-heat cooking oil; once used for saffron-like dye. Drought tolerant. Spiny varieties deter birds.
Large deciduous tree in the Juglandaceae family native to North America, producing rich, buttery nuts inside thin-shelled husks. Major commercial nut crop.
Also known as: Bluebeard. Compact shrub with blue flower clusters in late summer; silvery-gray foliage.
Majestic deciduous tree in the Fagaceae family producing starchy, edible nuts inside spiny burs. Important food tree across Europe and Asia for millennia.
Deciduous tree with enormous heart-shaped leaves, showy clusters of orchid-like white flowers, and long bean-like seed pods. Bold, tropical appearance in a hardy tree.

Also known as: Annual vinca, Rosy periwinkle, Cape periwinkle. Heat-loving bedding plant in the Apocynaceae family with glossy leaves and five-petaled flowers in pink, white, red, or purple all summer; not the trailing Vinca minor groundcover.
Majestic evergreen conifer with spreading, tiered branches and aromatic wood. The Cedar of Lebanon is one of the most culturally significant trees in history.
Massive tropical tree that can reach 60-70 meters with buttress roots and a wide canopy. Produces large pods containing silky, cotton-like fiber (kapok) used for stuffing and insulation.
Also known as: Cockscomb. Bold tropical annual with flower heads in distinctive plume, crest, or brain-like comb shapes; colors include brilliant red, orange, yellow, pink, and purple.
Also known as: Coontail, Rigid Hornwort. Fast-growing rootless aquatic plant that floats or can be anchored, excellent for nutrient absorption and algae control.
Small tree with magenta flowers on bare branches in early spring; heart-shaped leaves.
Large shrub or small tree with pink flowers on branches before leaves; more heat-tolerant than Eastern redbud.
Delicate trailing succulent with thin, needle-like leaves along wiry stems. Related to string of hearts but with a finer, more airy appearance.
Trailing succulent with heart-shaped leaves and purple undersides, produces tubers along stems.
Also known as: Japonica. Thorny deciduous shrub in the Rosaceae family that covers its bare branches with red, orange, pink, or white blossoms in late winter; small fragrant fruits make jelly.
Trailing plant with small white, pink, or blue flowers; ideal for hanging baskets and container edges.
Chamaedorea palm with pinnate fronds; cold-tolerant, can grow in ground in mild climates. Related to parlor palm.
Also known as: Reed palm. Clumping palm with bamboo-like stems and feathery fronds; ideal for low-light spaces and narrow corners.
Hardy, slow-growing palm with fan-shaped leaves, very low-maintenance and cold-tolerant.
Pseudo-cereal in the Amaranthaceae family. Gluten-free; complete protein. Tolerates salinity and drought. Rinse seeds to remove saponins.

Also known as: Japanese allspice, Làmei. Deciduous shrub in the Calycanthaceae family whose waxy, translucent yellow flowers open on bare stems in the depths of winter and release a powerful sweet fragrance; a treasured winter garden plant in China.
Also known as: Florist's chrysanthemum. Fall-blooming perennial flowering plants in the Asteraceae family, provide late-season color, many varieties available.
Annual legume in the Fabaceae family. Desi and kabuli types. Nutrient-dense pulse; drought tolerant. Cool-season crop.
Also known as: Frisée. Curly-leaved chicory in the Asteraceae family; slightly bitter, crisp leaves for salads. Distinct from escarole (broad-leaved).
Also known as: Broad-leaved endive. Broad-leaved chicory in the Asteraceae family; milder than curly endive, with flat, tender leaves for salads and cooking.

Also known as: Chioggia, Treviso, Castelfranco. Chicory in the Asteraceae family with bitter, wine-red leaves; forms compact heads. Essential in Italian cuisine; bitterness mellows when grilled or roasted.

Also known as: Camphor laurel. Massive, long-lived evergreen in the Lauraceae family with glossy aromatic leaves that smell of camphor when crushed; a revered street and temple tree in East Asia and the source of natural camphor, but invasive in Australia and the southern United States.
Tropical evergreen tree in the Lauraceae family whose inner bark is harvested and dried to produce one of the world's most important spices.
Tropical climbing vine with stunning elongated leaves featuring silver, green, and purple coloring with deep red-purple undersides, not a true begonia despite the common name.
Warm-season fruiting vegetable in the Cucurbitaceae family, large vining plants require space and a long growing season; yellow- and orange-fleshed cultivars are also grown.
Cultivar of watermelon in the Cucurbitaceae family with sweet yellow or orange flesh instead of red.

Also known as: Kaffir lime, Thai lime, Limau purut. Thorny citrus in the Rutaceae family grown for its glossy double-lobed leaves and knobbly green fruit rind, the signature aromatics of Thai curries, tom yum, and Indonesian cooking; the juice is scarce and bitter, so it is a leaf-and-zest tree.
Small citrus trees in the Rutaceae family, entire fruit is edible including peel, cold-hardier than most citrus.
Evergreen fruit trees in the Rutaceae family with fragrant flowers and edible fruits, require warm climates or indoor protection.
Also known as: Pummelo, Shaddock. Large citrus fruits in the Rutaceae family, largest citrus fruit, popular in China and Southeast Asia.
Also known as: Tangerine. Evergreen citrus tree producing easy-to-peel, sweet, segmented fruits. The most diverse citrus group and generally the most cold-hardy.
Evergreen citrus tree producing small, green, intensely tart fruits essential in cuisines worldwide. More cold-sensitive than lemons or oranges.

Also known as: Calamansi, Philippine lime, Calamondin orange. Small ornamental citrus, a natural kumquat and mandarin hybrid, that carries fragrant white flowers and tart, thin-skinned orange fruits almost year-round; a favorite indoor citrus and the souring agent of Filipino cooking.
Large evergreen citrus tree producing clusters of large, tangy-sweet fruits with pink, red, or white flesh. Needs sustained heat for sweetest fruit.
Climbing perennials in the Ranunculaceae family with large, showy flowers, require support and specific pruning.
Also known as: Spider flower. Tall, dramatic annual with spidery flower clusters in pink, purple, or white atop long stems, self-sowing freely for return displays.
Shade-tolerant flowering plant with strap-like leaves and striking orange or yellow flower clusters.
Tropical palm in the Arecaceae family producing large drupes with edible meat and water, requires warm coastal climate.
Also known as: Garden croton. Colorful tropical foliage plants in the Euphorbiaceae family with vibrant leaves in red, orange, yellow, and green, sensitive to changes.
Croton cultivar with twisted, spiral leaves in red, orange, yellow, and green.
Glossy-leaved shrub that can produce white flowers and red coffee cherries indoors.
Also known as: Painted nettle. Colorful foliage plants in the Lamiaceae family with vibrant leaves in various patterns and colors, pinch flowers to maintain foliage.
Trailing gesneriad with waxy, tubular flowers resembling goldfish in orange, red, or yellow; ideal for hanging baskets.
Annual herbaceous plant cultivated for its strong, biodegradable bast fiber — the second most important natural fiber after cotton. Known as the 'Golden Fiber' for its silky luster.
Tropical foliage plant with sword-shaped leaves in vibrant reds, pinks, purples, and greens. The Hawaiian ti plant holds deep cultural significance in Polynesian traditions.
Cheerful yellow daisies; long bloom season, low maintenance.
Deciduous trees and shrubs in the Cornaceae family with showy spring flowers and colorful fall foliage.
Also known as: Cobnut. Deciduous shrub or small tree in the Betulaceae family producing small, round edible nuts. Wind-pollinated with distinctive catkins in late winter.
Also known as: Garden cosmos. Annual flowers in the Asteraceae family with delicate, daisy-like blooms in shades of pink, white, and purple, easy to grow.
Shrub or small tree with fluffy gray-pink "smoke" plumes and purple or green foliage.
Spreading shrub with herringbone branches, small leaves, and red berries; groundcover or upright.
Fuzzy succulent with thick, toothed leaves resembling bear paws, tips turn red in bright light. Native to South Africa.
Succulents in the Crassulaceae family with thick fleshy leaves, many form tree-like structures over time.
Also known as: Compact jade, Mini jade. Compact jade plant cultivar with smaller leaves; same care as standard jade, ideal for small spaces.

Also known as: May tree, Thornapple, Quickthorn. Small thorny trees in the Rosaceae family with white or pink spring blossom and red autumn haws loved by birds; used as specimen trees, hedging, and in Chinese medicine (shanzha).
Also known as: Montbretia. Cormous perennial with arching stems of fiery funnel-shaped flowers in summer. 'Lucifer' is one of the bestselling garden plants worldwide.
Fall-blooming crocus. Red stigmas yield saffron spice. Dormant summer; leaves appear spring, flowers fall.
Early spring flowering bulbs in the Iridaceae family, among first flowers to bloom, naturalize well.
Also known as: Fishbone prayer plant. Prayer plants in the Marantaceae family with patterned leaves that fold up at night, more tolerant than some prayer plants.
Long, ribbed melon in the Cucurbitaceae family, eaten like cucumber when immature, mild and crisp, heat-tolerant.
Popular winter squash in the Cucurbitaceae family with sweet, nutty flavor, excellent for storage.
Also known as: Sweet potato squash. Cylindrical winter squash in the Cucurbitaceae family with creamy, sweet flesh and edible skin, stores well.
Small winter squash in the Cucurbitaceae family with acorn-shaped dark green fruits and sweet orange flesh, good for roasting.
Annual herb in the Apiaceae family cultivated for its small, aromatic seeds — the second most popular spice worldwide after black pepper. Essential in Indian, Mexican, and Middle Eastern cuisines.
Bright golden conifer with lemony scent, popular as indoor or patio plant, requires good air circulation.
Also known as: Pencil pine. Iconic narrow, columnar evergreen conifer with dark green, scale-like foliage; a defining element of Mediterranean and Tuscan landscapes.
Rhizomatous herbs in the Zingiberaceae family, related to ginger, popular spice and natural dye.
Trailing succulent with banana-shaped leaves, faster growing than String of Pearls.
Large genus of succulents in the Asteraceae family, includes trailing varieties like string of pearls (many reclassified to Curio).
Also known as: Dolphin Plant, Dolphin Succulent. Trailing succulent with leaves shaped like leaping dolphins.
Ancient cycad (not a true palm) with feathery fronds emerging from a woody trunk.
Tuberous flowering plants in the Primulaceae family with heart-shaped leaves and upswept flowers.
Deciduous tree in the Rosaceae family with aromatic golden pomes, must be cooked - ideal for preserves.

Also known as: Boat orchid. Terrestrial and semi-terrestrial orchids in the Orchidaceae family with grassy leaves and tall sprays of long-lasting waxy flowers in winter and spring; the big hybrids are florist staples, while the small Chinese species have been cultivated for their fragrance for over
Perennial thistle in the Asteraceae family, grown for edible flower buds before they bloom, Mediterranean origin.
Grass species maintained as lawns, require regular mowing and maintenance for healthy growth.
Cyperus (umbrella plant) for water gardens. Stems topped with umbel leaf whorls. Thrives in saturated soil or shallow water.
Tall marginal aquatic. Egyptian papyrus grows in shallow water or wet soil. Dramatic upright stems with fluffy tops.
Also known as: Garden dahlia. Tender tubers with showy summer flowers. Thousands of cultivars. Lift before frost; store dry over winter.
Seed-grown dahlia varieties treated as annuals, producing colorful single or semi-double flowers all summer without the need to store tubers over winter.
Compact, fragrant-flowering shrub prized for intensely sweet-scented winter and spring blooms. Among the most powerfully fragrant garden plants.
Vegetables grown for their edible underground parts, require loose well-drained soil for proper root development.
Root vegetables in the Apiaceae family, require deep, loose soil free of rocks for straight roots.

Also known as: Flamboyant, Flame tree, Gulmohar. Spreading tropical tree in the Fabaceae family with a flat umbrella crown of fern-like leaves that is smothered in scarlet-orange flowers for weeks in early summer; one of the most spectacular flowering trees in the world and a classic street tree of
Low-growing succulent groundcover with brilliant daisy-like flowers in neon pink, purple, orange, yellow, and white that open in full sun. Excellent for xeriscaping and dry slopes.
Cool-season annual with tall spikes of delphinium-like flowers in blue, purple, pink, or white, a cottage garden favorite and excellent cut flower.
Tall spikes of blue, purple, or white flowers; may need staking. Toxic.
Large orchid genus with cane-like stems and sprays of flowers. Many types: nobile (cool rest), phalaenopsis-type (warm), others. Epiphytic.
Tiny alpine pink with single flowers, often pink or white. Compact cushion form. Cold hardy, ideal for rock gardens.
Biennial to short-lived perennial in the Dianthus family, producing dense, flat-topped clusters of fragrant flowers in red, pink, white, and bicolor patterns.
Fringed flowers in pink, red, or white with spicy fragrance; compact form for borders and containers.
Also known as: Pinks. Compact plants with fragrant, fringed flowers; pinks, carnations, and sweet william.
Compact, bushy cultivar of dumb cane with variegated leaves; smaller than standard varieties, ideal for tabletops.
Also known as: Dumb cane. Cane-forming aroids with variegated foliage, toxic sap (handle with care).
Also known as: Dragon's eye. Evergreen fruit trees in the Sapindaceae family, related to lychee, require tropical or subtropical climate.

Also known as: True yam, Ñame, Ube. Tropical climbing vines in the Dioscoreaceae family grown for their large starchy tubers, a staple in West Africa, the Caribbean, and Asia; unrelated to the sweet potato often called yam in North America.
Deciduous fruit trees in the Ebenaceae family, astringent and non-astringent varieties, popular in both USA and China.
Also known as: String of nickels. Epiphytic succulents related to Hoya, with coin-shaped or heart-shaped leaves; trailing or climbing habit.
Also known as: African spear. Snake plant with cylindrical, spear-like leaves; often braided when young. Same drought tolerance as flat-leaf varieties.

Iconic umbrella-shaped tree endemic to Socotra Island, Yemen. Known for its distinctive mushroom-like canopy and crimson red resin (dragon's blood) used in traditional medicine and dyes for centuries.
Also known as: Limelight dracaena. Bright lime-green cultivar of Dracaena fragrans (Deremensis Group); adds vivid color to low-light spaces.
Also known as: Corn plant. Corn plant with broad, arching leaves, can grow quite tall. Includes the popular 'Janet Craig' (Deremensis Group) and 'Massangeana' cultivars.
Also known as: Striped dracaena. Stripe-edged dracaena with green and white or cream variegation; upright growth habit.
Also known as: Zebra-striped dragon tree. Rare dracaena with striking horizontal zebra-like bands of dark and light green on broad, oval leaves. A trending collector plant.
Compact dracaena with yellow-edged leaves in a spiral arrangement; slow-growing and compact.
Also known as: Dragon tree, Madagascar dragon tree. Dragon tree with thin, arching leaves with red edges, very low-maintenance.
Also known as: Chinese water bamboo. Dracaena species often grown in water or soil, popular for feng shui, not a true bamboo.

Also known as: Mother-in-law's tongue. Extremely low-maintenance succulents in the Asparagaceae family with upright sword-like leaves. Includes various cultivars with different leaf shapes and patterns.
Also known as: Golden hahnii. Dwarf snake plant with rosette-forming leaves; compact, ideal for small spaces and tabletops.
Snake plant with silvery-gray, broad leaves; subtle banding. Same easy care as other Dracaena trifasciata varieties.
Also known as: Drosera. Carnivorous plants in the Droseraceae family with sticky, dewy leaves that trap insects.
Popular tropical sundew from South Africa, easy to grow and forgiving of beginners. No dormancy required. Produces tall flower stalks and abundant sticky dew.
Legendary tropical fruit famous for its custard-like flesh and notoriously pungent aroma—banned on public transport across Southeast Asia but revered as a delicacy.
Annual herb in the Amaranthaceae family with a pungent, medicinal flavor. Traditional in Mexican bean dishes to reduce gas. Used sparingly due to strong flavor.
Hybrid echeveria with lavender-pink rosettes; powdery farina. Non-toxic to pets.
Also known as: PVN. Popular echeveria with purple-pink rosettes and powdery farina; classic succulent. Non-toxic to pets.
Yellow-petaled Echinacea species native to the Ozarks; drought tolerant prairie wildflower.
Also known as: Coneflower, Purple coneflower. Hardy native perennial with daisy-like flowers featuring a prominent spiny central cone, popular with pollinators.
Architectural perennial with spherical, steel-blue flower heads and spiny, silvery-gray foliage. The national flower of Scotland (Cirsium thistle). Excellent for dried flower arrangements.
Round or columnar cacti that produce large, funnel-shaped flowers in white, pink, or red, often opening at night.
European wildflower with blue coiled flower spikes; biennial or short-lived perennial; full sun.
Tropical palm cultivated for its fruit, which yields palm oil — the world's most widely used vegetable oil. Extremely productive: produces more oil per hectare than any other crop.
Also known as: Green cardamom. Spice plant in the ginger family with aromatic seeds used in cooking and chai.
Epiphytic woodland cactus with flat, leaf-like stems that produce spectacular nocturnal flowers in many colors.
Also known as: Devil's ivy. Most common pothos variety with green and yellow variegated leaves, extremely easy-care.
Also known as: Green pothos. Solid green pothos with no variegation; most tolerant of low light and the hardiest pothos variety.
Pothos variety with white and green marbled variegation, requires more light than golden pothos to maintain variegation.
Also known as: Lime pothos. Vibrant chartreuse pothos variety with solid bright green-yellow leaves, adds bright color to indoor spaces.
Unique pothos cultivar with curled and twisted leaves that give a compact, textured appearance. Same easy care as standard pothos but with distinctive ruffled foliage.
Highly variegated pothos with white and green leaves; develops fenestrations when mature. Same care as Cebu Blue.
Pothos variety with silvery-blue, elongated leaves; develops fenestrations when mature. Same easy care as golden pothos.
Ancient, primitive plant with hollow, jointed, bamboo-like stems and no true leaves or flowers. A living fossil — horsetails date back over 350 million years to the Carboniferous period.
Annual grass in the Poaceae family. Tiny gluten-free grain; staple in Ethiopia. Drought tolerant. Seeds minuscule—harvest carefully.
Also known as: Chinese plum. Evergreen fruit trees in the Rosaceae family with sweet, tangy fruits, popular in China and Japan.
Elegant fall-blooming perennials with simple pink or white flowers on tall, wiry stems, thriving in partial shade where few other plants flower in autumn.
Also known as: Rocket, Roquette. Fast-growing leafy green in the Brassicaceae family with peppery flavor, also known as rocket or roquette.
Peppery microgreens from arugula seeds. Fast-growing. Harvest at first true leaves (7–10 days).
Prairie native with yucca-like leaves and spherical white flower clusters; drought tolerant.

Also known as: Cider gum. Fast-growing evergreen trees native to Australia with aromatic, often silvery-blue foliage and distinctive peeling bark; widely planted for timber, ornamental value, and essential oil.
Shrub with corky winged branches; brilliant scarlet fall color; invasive in many areas.
Versatile genus of evergreen and deciduous shrubs used extensively in landscaping for hedging, groundcover, and specimen planting. Includes the fiery-red burning bush.
Thorny succulent shrub with colorful bracts that bloom year-round in bright light.
Also known as: Cathedral cactus. Candelabra-shaped succulent with green stems and leaves; milky sap is toxic—handle with care.
Also known as: Texas bluebell. Elegant annual or short-lived perennial producing ruffled, rose-like blooms in white, pink, purple, and bicolor; prized as a premium cut flower.
Prized in Japanese cuisine for its pungent, sinus-clearing flavor. Notoriously difficult to grow — requires cool, shady, humid conditions with clean running water.
Also known as: Sweet Joe Pye. Tall native with pink-purple flower clusters; prefers moist to wet soil; butterfly magnet.
Pseudo-cereal in the Polygonaceae family. Gluten-free; fast-growing cover crop. White flowers attract pollinators. Short season (70–90 days).
Deciduous tree with smooth, silver-gray bark and glossy oval leaves that turn golden-bronze in autumn. Copper beech is a prized ornamental with purple foliage.

Also known as: Pineapple guava, Guavasteen. Evergreen shrub or small tree in the Myrtaceae family with silvery leaves, edible red-and-white flowers, and green egg-shaped fruits that taste of pineapple, guava, and mint; a backyard staple in New Zealand and a tough ornamental hedge.
Compact ornamental grass with blue-gray foliage; forms neat mounds, ideal for borders and rock gardens.
Tall fig tree with leathery, variegated leaves in shades of green and yellow. Also called council tree. Easier to care for than fiddle leaf fig.
The more forgiving cousin of the Fiddle Leaf Fig, with velvety, oval leaves and pale trunk, increasingly popular as a statement houseplant.
Deciduous fruit trees in the Moraceae family, can be grown in containers, some varieties produce two crops.
Popular ficus with large, glossy dark green or burgundy leaves, can grow into a tree.
Ficus elastica cultivar with dark burgundy, nearly black leaves; bold statement plant.
Striking Ficus elastica cultivar with tricolored leaves in deep green, cream, and vivid ruby-pink, especially vibrant on new growth.
Variegated rubber plant cultivar with striking cream, green, and pink-edged leaves, more colorful than the standard rubber plant while retaining its easy-care nature.
Also known as: FLF. Popular but finicky ficus with large violin-shaped leaves, requires consistent care and stable environment.
Ficus with glossy oval leaves, popular for bonsai; can develop aerial roots.
Also known as: Sacred Fig, Peepal Tree, Pipal. Tropical fig tree sacred in Buddhism, with distinctive heart-shaped leaves and long drip tips.
Also known as: Mosaic plant. Colorful foliage plants in the Acanthaceae family with distinctive veining in various colors, will wilt dramatically when thirsty.
Also known as: Finocchio. Bulb vegetables in the Apiaceae family with licorice flavor, both bulb and fronds are edible.
One of the earliest spring-blooming shrubs, covered in bright yellow flowers before leaves emerge. Fast-growing and hardy; often used as hedging or specimen plants.
Also known as: Garden strawberry. Low-growing perennial berry plants in the Rosaceae family, produce runners for propagation.
Deciduous tree with compound leaves and winged seeds (samaras). Valued for its strong, flexible wood used in tool handles, furniture, and baseball bats. Currently threatened by emerald ash borer.
Fragrant spring corms. Plant in fall (mild climates) or spring. Tubular flowers in many colors. Tender—lift in cold zones.
Also known as: Snake's head. Spring bulbs with nodding, checkered or crown-shaped flowers. Snake's head (F. meleagris) and crown imperial. Plant in fall.
Graceful flowering plants with pendulous, lantern-shaped blooms in vivid combinations of pink, purple, red, and white. The quintessential hanging basket and shade garden plant.
Also known as: Blanket Flower. Colorful daisy-like perennials and annuals with red, yellow, and orange bicolor flowers. Drought tolerant and long-blooming, excellent for pollinators.
One of the earliest spring bulbs, often blooming through snow. Dainty nodding white flowers with green markings appear from late winter to early spring.
Low-growing shade groundcover with whorls of bright green leaves and tiny white star-shaped spring flowers. Dried leaves have sweet vanilla-hay scent; traditional flavoring for May wine.
Tongue-shaped succulents closely related to Haworthia and Aloe in the family Asphodelaceae; shade-tolerant and easy-care.

Also known as: Treasure flower. Low, sun-loving South African daisy in the Asteraceae family with large, boldly striped flowers in orange, yellow, red, pink, and bronze that open in sun and close at night and on cloudy days.
Evergreen vine with fragrant yellow trumpet flowers in early spring; state flower of South Carolina.
Also known as: Gentiana. Alpine and woodland plants in the Gentianaceae family with intense blue flowers, prefer cool, moist conditions.
Striking tropical plant with deeply textured, dark purple-black suckered leaves that shimmer in the light. A trending collector plant.
European geranium with blue-violet flowers; long blooming; low maintenance.
Also known as: Cranesbill. True perennial geraniums with cup-shaped flowers and rounded leaves; low-maintenance groundcover for borders.
Also known as: Maidenhair tree. Ancient deciduous trees in the Ginkgoaceae family, living fossil, popular street tree in China, male and female trees.
Also known as: Garden gladiolus. Summer flowering bulbs in the Iridaceae family with tall spikes of colorful flowers, excellent for cut flowers.

Also known as: Tong ho, Shungiku, Crown daisy, Chop suey greens. Cool-season leafy vegetable in the Asteraceae family with aromatic, slightly bitter leaves used in hot pot, stir-fries, and sukiyaki; small yellow daisies appear if left to bolt.

Also known as: Green soybean. Immature soybeans harvested while still green and tender (leave pods to mature and dry for dry soybeans), a popular snack and ingredient in East Asian cuisine. Higher in protein than most vegetables.
Compact prayer plant with light green leaves featuring bold dark green striping along the veins; folds leaves upward at night.
Prayer plant with delicate white pinstripes on bright green, elliptical leaves. More compact than Calathea ornata with finer, more numerous stripes.
Prayer plant with wavy, patterned leaves resembling a rattlesnake's tail.
Stunning prayer plant with an intricate mosaic-like network pattern on its leaves that resembles stained glass or circuit boards, one of the most visually complex leaf patterns in nature.
Prayer plant with variegated leaves in white, green, and lavender; leaves fold up at night.
Prayer plant with bold white stripes on dark green leaves; leaves fold up at night.
Also known as: Peacock plant, Cathedral windows. Prayer plant with oval leaves featuring peacock-like patterns, leaves fold up at night.
Also known as: Round-leaved calathea. Large prayer plant with silver-striped round leaves, requires high humidity, leaves fold up at night (nyctinasty).
Also known as: Pin-stripe plant. Elegant prayer plant with dark green, glossy leaves adorned with thin pink or white pinstripes that fade to cream with age.
Also known as: Rose painted calathea. Prayer plant with oval leaves featuring a bold pink or cream border on dark green, with purple undersides. Multiple popular cultivars.
Popular prayer plant with dark green leaves and purple undersides, requires high humidity, leaves fold up at night.
Prayer plant with velvety stripes alternating dark and light green; leaves fold up at night.

Also known as: Bachelor's button (not to be confused with Centaurea). Heat-loving annual producing round, clover-like flower heads in magenta, purple, white, pink, and red that hold their color when dried.
Annual shrub in the Malvaceae family. Grown for fiber (lint) and seed oil. Warm-season; needs long frost-free period. Upland and Pima types.
Also known as: Mother-of-pearl plant. Succulents in the Crassulaceae family with rosette-forming leaves, often called ghost plants.
Tropical plants in the Bromeliaceae family with rosette growth and central cups (tanks) that hold water.
Colorful bromeliads with bright, long-lasting flower spikes.
Also known as: Moon cactus. Small, round cacti with chin-like notches above each areole; Moon cactus is a colorful grafted form.

Also known as: Velvet plant, Purple velvet plant, Gynura. Trailing houseplant in the Asteraceae family whose green leaves are covered in iridescent purple hairs that glow in bright light; the small orange flowers smell unpleasant and are usually pinched off.
Graceful, cascading grass with gold or green variegation; thrives in shade.
Deciduous shrub or small tree that blooms in late winter to early spring with fragrant, spidery, ribbon-like flowers in yellow, orange, or red when most other plants are dormant.
Small rosette succulents that tolerate lower light than most succulents, perfect for windowsills.
Also known as: Helen's flower. Late-summer to fall perennial with daisy-like flowers in warm tones of yellow, orange, red, and bicolor, featuring distinctive raised central cones.
Annual and perennial flowers in the Asteraceae family with large, cheerful yellow blooms that follow the sun.
Prairie native with tall stems of yellow flowers; spreads by rhizomes; bird and pollinator favorite.
Also known as: Sunchoke. Perennial sunflower relative in the Asteraceae family, grown for edible tubers (sunchokes), nutty flavor, can spread readily.
Tropical rhizomatous plants with spectacular waxy bracts in red, orange, yellow, and pink. Related to banana and bird of paradise.
Also known as: Lenten rose. Shade-loving perennials that bloom in late winter to early spring with nodding flowers in white, pink, purple, green, or burgundy.
Also known as: Daylily. Hardy perennial flowering plants in the Asphodelaceae family, each flower lasts one day but plants produce many blooms.
Tropical shrub with glossy, palmately compound leaves—leaflets radiate from a central point like umbrella ribs.
Compact umbrella plant with palmate leaves, easier to manage indoors than the larger schefflera.
Also known as: Coral Bells. Versatile shade-loving perennial grown primarily for its colorful foliage in shades of purple, bronze, lime, peach, and silver. Delicate bell-shaped flowers on wiry stems.
Tropical tree in the Euphorbiaceae family, the primary source of natural rubber (latex). Not to be confused with Ficus elastica (rubber plant houseplant).
Also known as: Rose mallow. Cold-hardy perennial hibiscus producing dinner-plate-sized flowers (up to 30 cm) in white, pink, red, and bicolor from mid-summer to frost.
Also known as: Chinese hibiscus. Showy shrub with large, colorful trumpet flowers that last one day but bloom repeatedly.
Large flowering bulbs in the Amaryllidaceae family, popular for indoor winter forcing, can rebloom with proper care.
Annual grass in the Poaceae family. Cereal grain for malt, feed, and food. Spring and winter types. Tolerates cooler climates than wheat.
Also known as: Funkia. Shade-loving perennial foliage plants in the Asparagaceae family, grown for their attractive leaves in various colors and sizes.
Vining Hoya with waxy, oval leaves and fragrant white flowers with red centers.
Distinctive Hoya species with long, pointed leaves featuring prominent dark veining on a light green background, giving a stained-glass appearance. A highly sought-after collector Hoya.
Hoya carnosa cultivar with twisted, curled leaves creating a rope-like appearance; Hindu rope.
Also known as: Variegated wax plant. Popular variegated Hoya carnosa cultivar with creamy white to pink margins on waxy, semi-succulent leaves.
Compact Hoya species with small, thick oval leaves and fragrant yellow star-shaped flower clusters. One of the easier Hoyas to bring into bloom.
Trailing Hoya with small, silver-mottled leaves; ideal for hanging baskets.
Compact, trailing hoya with small, pointed leaves and clusters of star-shaped, fragrant white flowers with pink or purple centers. One of the most popular hoyas for hanging baskets.
Trailing Hoya with long, narrow, fuzzy leaves; pendulous habit suits hanging baskets.
Compact Hoya with silver-flecked leaves; hybrid of H. serpens × H. carnosa.
Large, round-leaved Hoya with thick, often silver-splashed foliage. Splash markings are the standard form. Produces fragrant star-shaped flower clusters.
Fast-growing Hoya with silver-flecked leaves and fragrant dark pink or red flowers.
Trailing hoya with narrow, elongated leaves edged in red or dark maroon, producing clusters of fragrant star-shaped flowers when mature.

Also known as: English bluebell, Wood hyacinth. Spring bulbs in the Asparagaceae family that carpet woodlands with nodding violet-blue bells; the English species is protected in the UK, and the vigorous Spanish species and hybrids can take over gardens.
Woody shrubs grown primarily for their flowers, many require specific soil pH for optimal bloom color.
Deciduous vine with lacecap flowers and aerial roots; slow to establish but vigorous once rooted.
Also known as: Mophead, Lacecap. Popular flowering shrubs in the Hydrangeaceae family, flower color depends on soil pH for some varieties.
Panicle hydrangea with large, cone-shaped flower clusters that emerge lime-green, turn white, then fade to pink in fall. Blooms on new wood, so reliable even after harsh winters.
Also known as: Stonecrop. Hardy succulent perennials with fleshy leaves and clusters of star-shaped flowers. Includes tall upright types and low-growing groundcovers. Extremely drought tolerant.
Subtropical holly tree native to South America whose leaves are brewed into mate — a traditional caffeinated beverage central to the culture of Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay, and southern Brazil.
Evergreen or deciduous shrub with spiny leaves and red berries; needs male and female for fruit.
Also known as: Busy Lizzie. Shade-loving annual flowering plants in the Balsaminaceae family with colorful blooms, excellent for shady areas.
Vigorous tropical vine with large, fragrant, pure white flowers that open at dusk and close at dawn. The nocturnal companion to morning glory.
Also known as: Kangkong. Semi-aquatic vine in the Convolvulaceae family; hollow stems and tender leaves. Staples in Southeast Asian and Chinese cooking.
Fast-growing annual and perennial vines in the Convolvulaceae family with trumpet-shaped flowers that open in morning.
Perennial flowering plants in the Iridaceae family with distinctive sword-like leaves and showy flowers, include bearded and beardless types.
Iris species adapted to wet conditions, grow in shallow water or boggy soil, ideal for water gardens.
Hybrid spring bulb with slender stems and elegant flowers in blue, purple, white, or yellow. Plant in fall for spring bloom; goes dormant after flowering.
Deciduous to semi-evergreen tropical tree famous for spectacular violet-blue flower clusters that blanket the canopy in spring. Iconic street tree worldwide.
Also known as: Silver ragwort. Silver-foliage annual (perennial in mild climates) grown for its deeply lobed, felt-textured, silvery-white leaves that provide contrast in borders and containers.
Also known as: Pink jasmine. Fragrant flowering vines in the Oleaceae family, popular for their sweet-smelling blooms.
Deciduous nut tree in the Juglandaceae family producing edible walnuts in hard shells, valued for both nuts and premium timber.
Evergreen coniferous shrubs and trees in the Cupressaceae family, drought-tolerant and versatile for landscapes.

Also known as: Flaming Katy, Florist Kalanchoe. Colorful succulent houseplants with clusters of long-lasting blooms in red, pink, orange, yellow, and white. The most popular species is K. blossfeldiana.
Also known as: Flapjack. Succulent with flat, paddle-shaped leaves that blush red at edges in bright light; monocarpic (dies after flowering).
European wildflower with lavender pincushion flowers; long blooming; attracts butterflies.
Striking architectural perennials with dense, torch-like flower spikes in fiery shades of red, orange, and yellow. Native to southern Africa.
Desert plants in the Cactaceae family with spines and areoles, need excellent drainage and bright light.
Also known as: Golden barrel cactus. Round, barrel-shaped cacti that can grow quite large, very low-maintenance.

Also known as: Lablab, Dolichos bean, Egyptian bean, Indian bean. Vigorous twining vine in the Fabaceae family grown as an ornamental for its purple-tinged leaves, fragrant lilac pea flowers, and glossy magenta pods, and as a vegetable in Asia and Africa for its young pods and cooked beans.
Vegetables grown primarily for their edible leaves. Many are cool-season crops that bolt in heat. Quick to harvest and ideal for successive planting.

Also known as: Calabash, Opo squash, Lauki, Dudhi. Vigorous annual vine in the Cucurbitaceae family with white night-opening flowers; young fruits are a mild cooking vegetable across Asia and Africa, and mature fruits dry into hard-shelled containers and birdhouses.
Also known as: Lamium. Low-growing shade groundcover with silver-marked, heart-shaped leaves and small hooded flowers in pink, purple, or white. Not a true nettle — does not sting.
Also known as: Old-fashioned bleeding heart. Graceful heart-shaped flowers on arching stems; foliage goes dormant in summer heat.
Unique deciduous conifer that sheds its needles in autumn after turning brilliant golden-yellow. Fresh green spring foliage is remarkably soft. Native to cold, mountainous regions.
Beloved annual climbing flower prized for its fragrant, ruffled blooms in a wide range of pastel colors. A cottage garden classic.
Also known as: English lavender. Aromatic flowering herbs in the Lamiaceae family with silvery foliage and fragrant purple flowers, drought-tolerant once established.
Tiny floating plants. Rapid spread; provides shade and filtration. Can be invasive. Often used in aquariums and small ponds.
Annual legume in the Fabaceae family. Small lenticular seeds—red, green, brown. High protein pulse. Cool-season; drought tolerant.
Iconic alpine plant in the Asteraceae family with woolly white flowers, symbol of the Alps, requires excellent drainage.
Peppery, fast-growing sprouts. Harvest in 5–7 days. Can grow on paper towel.
Daisy-like flowering plants in the Asteraceae family, include both annual and perennial types with white or colored petals.
Classic white daisy-like flowers with golden yellow centers; reliable, long-blooming garden perennial.
Also known as: Bitterroot. Alpine succulents with rosettes and showy flowers in pink, magenta, or white. Needs sharp drainage; crown must stay dry.
Prairie native with tall purple flower spikes; attracts butterflies and pollinators; drought tolerant.
Also known as: Lily. Bulbous perennial flowering plants in the Liliaceae family with showy trumpet-shaped or recurved flowers, many are fragrant.
Fragrant late-summer lilies. Large, often spotted flowers. Stargazer and Casablanca types. Toxic to cats.
Orange Turk's-cap lily with black spots. Lilium lancifolium. Naturalizes; can spread. Toxic to cats.
Also known as: Wavyleaf statice. Papery, brightly colored flower clusters on wiry stems; a classic everlasting flower prized for fresh and dried arrangements.
Annual in the Linaceae family. Grown for fiber (linen) and seeds (linseed oil, omega-3). Blue flowers. Cool-season crop.
Tall deciduous tree with star-shaped leaves and spiky seed balls; brilliant fall color.
Also known as: Lichi. Evergreen fruit trees in the Sapindaceae family with sweet, fragrant fruits, require tropical or subtropical climate.
Stone-like succulents that mimic pebbles in their native habitat, have specific dormancy periods when they should not be watered.
Mounding or trailing plant with masses of small blue, white, or pink flowers; cools down in heat but rebounds in fall.
Also known as: Sweet alyssum. Low mounds of tiny white, pink, or purple flowers with honey fragrance; ideal for edges and containers.
Climbing and shrubby plants in the Caprifoliaceae family with fragrant, tubular flowers, some species can be invasive.
Native vine with red or orange tubular flowers; non-invasive alternative to Japanese honeysuckle.
Also known as: Chinese fringe flower. Shrub with purple or green foliage and fringed white or pink flowers; related to witch hazel.
Also known as: Loofah. Gourd vine in the Cucurbitaceae family; young fruit edible as vegetable; mature fruit dries into natural sponge.
Also known as: Garden lupine. Tall spikes of pea-like flowers in blue, purple, pink, yellow, and bicolors; nitrogen-fixing perennial that enriches soil.
Also known as: Wolfberry. Deciduous shrubs in the Solanaceae family, also known as wolfberry, popular superfood, drought-tolerant.
Also known as: Moneywort. Fast-spreading groundcover with round, coin-shaped leaves. Golden variety (Aurea) is one of the most popular container and hanging basket trailing plants.
Deciduous and evergreen trees in the Magnoliaceae family with large, fragrant flowers, many species are ancient flowering plants.
Deciduous and evergreen trees grown for edible fruits, require proper pruning and often need cross-pollination.
Small flowering tree with spring blossoms and persistent ornamental fruit; many disease-resistant cultivars.
Round, woolly cactus covered in white hairs, produces pink flowers.
Compact, round cacti with spiral tubercles and a crown of small flowers in spring.
Vining plant with trumpet flowers in pink, red, or white; blooms from spring through fall.
Tropical tree in the Anacardiaceae family with sweet orange-fleshed drupes, widely cultivated fruit.
Also known as: Manioc, Yuca, Tapioca. Tropical root crop and staple food for over 800 million people worldwide. Produces starchy tuberous roots used for flour, tapioca, and animal feed.
Also known as: Herringbone plant. Classic prayer plant with red-veined leaves that fold up at night.
Herb in the Asteraceae family with daisy-like flowers used for soothing tea. German chamomile is annual; Roman chamomile is perennial. Both have apple-scented foliage.

Also known as: Common stock. Sweetly fragrant cool-season annual or biennial with dense spikes of double or single flowers in white, pink, purple, red, and cream; prized for its intoxicating clove-like scent.
Perennial legume in the Fabaceae family. Major forage crop for hay and grazing. Nitrogen-fixing; deep roots. Also grown for sprouting.
Also known as: Rose Grape. Dramatic tropical houseplant with large, leathery leaves and cascading clusters of pink flowers that can last for months.
Perennial herbs in the Lamiaceae family with aromatic leaves, can be invasive, spreads by runners.
Vigorous aromatic herb with dark green leaves edged in purple and a strong, cooling menthol flavor used in teas, desserts, cocktails, and herbal remedies.
Deciduous conifer discovered in China in 1944, previously known only from fossils, with feathery foliage that turns russet-bronze in autumn.
Australian native fern with glossy, lobed fronds; easy-care, tolerant of drier air than most ferns.
Fern with textured, reptilian-pattern fronds; tropical appearance. Medium humidity preferred.
One of the most popular beginner aquarium plants, grows attached to rocks and driftwood rather than planted in substrate.
Old-fashioned garden plant with trumpet-shaped flowers that open in late afternoon and stay open through the night. Single plant can produce flowers of different colors simultaneously.
Tall ornamental grass with silvery plumes and arching foliage; can be invasive.
Tropical gourd in the Cucurbitaceae family with warty, bitter fruits, popular in Asian cuisine for medicinal and culinary use.
Also known as: Bergamot. Native perennial with shaggy red, pink, or purple flowers; aromatic foliage.
Native bee balm with lavender flowers; aromatic foliage; drought tolerant; attracts pollinators.
Also known as: Swiss cheese vine. Swiss cheese vine with smaller, perforated leaves compared to Monstera deliciosa.
Variegated Monstera with white sections on green leaves; highly sought after. Requires bright light to maintain variegation.
Variegated Monstera with yellow-gold splashes on green leaves; similar care to Albo but different coloration.
Tissue-culture variegated Monstera with cream splashes; more stable variegation than Albo. Highly sought after.
Climbing Monstera species with elongated, lance-shaped leaves that develop small fenestrations (holes) as they mature, more compact than M. deliciosa.
Also known as: Silver monstera. Silver-marked Monstera with juvenile leaves that develop fenestrations when mature. Climbing habit.

Rare climbing Monstera with dramatically large fenestrations that give leaves a skeleton-like appearance. Long sold as Monstera epipremnoides, but now treated as a distinct, as yet undescribed species.
Climbing Monstera with deeply textured, quilted leaves; no fenestrations. Distinct from M. deliciosa.
Smaller Monstera species with elongated oval leaves featuring cream or yellow variegation (spots and splashes), a climbing vine often confused with Philodendron.
Fast-growing, drought-tolerant tree with edible leaves, pods, seeds, and flowers. Extremely nutritious — leaves contain high levels of vitamins and minerals.
Deciduous tree in the Moraceae family with sweet black, red, or white berry-like fruits, fast-growing.
Ornamental grass with airy pink to purple clouds of flowers in fall; drought tolerant, striking display.
Tropical herb in the Musaceae family producing bunches of sweet fruits, each stem fruits once then is replaced by suckers.
Also known as: Cooking Banana, Plátano. Large tropical herbaceous plant producing starchy, thick-skinned fruits used as a cooked vegetable staple worldwide.
Also known as: Woodland Forget-Me-Not, Scorpion Grass. Charming biennial with clusters of tiny sky-blue flowers and a heart-shaped petal arrangement.
Tropical evergreen tree in the Myristicaceae family producing two spices from one fruit: nutmeg (from the seed) and mace (from the red aril surrounding it).
Also known as: Jonquil. Spring-blooming bulbous perennials in the Amaryllidaceae family, planted in fall, naturalize well and are deer-resistant.

Also known as: Sacred Lotus, Indian Lotus. Aquatic perennial with iconic round leaves and showy flowers rising above the water. Edible roots (lotus root), seeds, and leaves widely used in Asian cuisine. Spiritual significance in many cultures.
Tank bromeliads with colorful central cups that hold water. Leaves form a rosette; flowers emerge from the center. Epiphytic in nature.
Tropical pitcher plants (monkey cups) from Southeast Asia with hanging pitcher traps. Highlanders and lowlanders have different temperature needs.
Mounding perennial with lavender-blue flower spikes; aromatic, cat-attracting foliage.
Tropical fruit tree producing clusters of hairy red or yellow fruits with translucent, sweet, lychee-like flesh inside—the name comes from the Malay word for hair.
Compact Boston fern relative with small, round leaflets; lemony scent. More forgiving than standard Boston fern.

Also known as: Flowering tobacco, Jasmine tobacco. Ornamental relatives of tobacco in the Solanaceae family with sticky leaves and tubular, star-faced flowers in white, lime green, pink, and red; the tall species release a heady jasmine scent at dusk for moths.
Annual herb in the Solanaceae family. Leaves contain nicotine; grown for commercial tobacco. Ornamental Nicotiana species differ. Not for consumption.
Classic floating aquatic. Leaves and flowers float on surface. Plant in pots at pond bottom. Hardy and tropical types.
Also known as: Tulsi. Annual herb in the Lamiaceae family, sacred in Hinduism. Aromatic leaves with clove-like flavor used in Thai cuisine and Ayurvedic medicine. Different from sweet basil.
Also known as: Bee blossom. Graceful perennial with slender, wiry stems bearing delicate white or pink flowers that dance in the breeze from late spring to frost.
Evergreen tree in the Oleaceae family producing drupes for oil and table olives, Mediterranean origin.
Epiphytic orchids with spray-like flower stems, often yellow "dancing lady" blossoms. Includes many intergeneric hybrids (Oncostele, etc.).
Low-growing evergreen groundcover with fine, dark green grass-like foliage, including the dramatic black-leaved variety used as an accent in modern gardens.
Flat-padded cacti in the Opuntia genus, can produce edible fruit, very low-maintenance.
Flat-padded cactus with glochids (tiny barbed spines) instead of large spines; handle with care.
Also known as: Wild marjoram. Perennial herbs in the Lamiaceae family with pungent leaves, essential in Mediterranean cuisine.
Annual grass in the Poaceae family. Staple grain grown in flooded paddies (lowland) or upland. Short-grain, long-grain, and aromatic varieties.
Also known as: Sweet osmanthus. Evergreen shrubs in the Oleaceae family with highly fragrant flowers, popular in Chinese gardens and tea.

Also known as: Cape daisy, Osteospermum. Bushy South African daisies in the Asteraceae family with flowers in white, purple, pink, yellow, orange, and bicolors, often with a steel-blue center; they bloom heaviest in the cool of spring and autumn and close at night.
Trailing succulent with bean-shaped leaves that turn deep ruby-red in bright light; stems are purple-tinged.
Plants in the Oxalidaceae family with clover-like leaves that fold at night, some species go dormant seasonally.
Also known as: Moonstones. Adorable succulents with plump, egg-shaped leaves in pastel shades of lavender, pink, and blue-grey, often covered in a powdery farina coating.
Evergreen groundcover in the Buxaceae family with glossy leaves, excellent for shady areas and erosion control.
Herbaceous and tree perennials in the Paeoniaceae family with large, fragrant flowers in spring, long-lived garden favorites.
Woody shrub peony producing enormous, ruffled flowers (15-25cm across) in spring. Called the 'King of Flowers' in Chinese culture with over 1,500 years of cultivation.
Also known as: Asian Ginseng, Korean Ginseng, Red Ginseng. Slow-growing woodland herb prized for its fleshy root used in traditional medicine for centuries.

Also known as: Screwpine, Pandanus, Daun pandan. Clumping tropical plant in the Pandanaceae family with long, strap-like fragrant leaves that flavor rice, desserts, and drinks across Southeast Asia, giving a sweet, grassy, vanilla-like aroma and a natural green color.
Annual grass in the Poaceae family. Proso (common) millet and others. Gluten-free grain; drought tolerant. Short season (60–90 days).
Tall native prairie grass with airy flower panicles; blue-green or red cultivars; important biofuel crop.
Iconic flowering plants with papery, crepe-like petals in vibrant reds, oranges, yellows, and pinks. Includes annual and perennial species. California poppy is the state flower of California.

Also known as: Lady's slipper orchid. Terrestrial orchids prized for their distinctive pouch-shaped lip that traps pollinating insects, with blooms in rich earth tones, greens, and dramatic spotted or striped patterns.
Round, ribbed cacti that produce yellow or golden flowers from the crown.
Deciduous vine with five leaflets; spectacular red fall color, often confused with poison ivy.
Deciduous vine with three-lobed leaves that turn brilliant red in fall; clings to walls via adhesive pads.
Exotic vines with intricate purple, blue, or white flowers; some species produce edible passion fruit.
Tropical vine in the Passifloraceae family with tart-sweet purple or yellow fruits, exotic flavor.
Root vegetables in the Apiaceae family, flavor improves after frost, require long growing season.
Also known as: Zonal geranium. Popular annual and perennial flowering plants, include zonal geraniums (Pelargonium) and true geraniums (hardy geraniums).
Ornamental grass with bottlebrush flower plumes; arching foliage in green, burgundy, or variegated.
Also known as: Beardtongue. Tubular flowers on upright stems in many colors; native North American perennial, drought-tolerant, attracts hummingbirds.
Star-shaped flower clusters in red, pink, or white; butterfly magnet, heat-loving.
Compact peperomia with deeply ridged, dark green leaves and striking red undersides. Semi-succulent with low water needs. Excellent desk plant.
Also known as: Rainbow edge peperomia. Compact peperomia with tricolor leaves—green, cream, and pink edges; upright growth habit.
Also known as: Turtle vine. Trailing peperomia with small, patterned leaves resembling turtle shells, slower growing than other string plants.
Annual herb in the Lamiaceae family with a mint-basil flavor. Green and red varieties used in Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese cuisine. Essential for sushi and banchan.
Perennial herb in the Polygonaceae family with spicy, cilantro-like flavor. Essential in Vietnamese pho and salads. Not a true coriander; thrives in warm, moist conditions.
Large, trumpet-shaped flowers in many colors; showy but sensitive to rain and heat.
Also known as: Moth orchid. Moth orchids, most common and beginner-friendly orchid genus in the Orchidaceae family with long-lasting blooms. Available in various colors.
Fast-growing legume vegetables in the Fabaceae family, from snap and shelling beans to lima and runner beans; pole types need support while bush types are self-supporting.
Also known as: Sweet mock orange, English dogwood. Deciduous shrub in the Hydrangeaceae family grown for its masses of white, intensely orange-blossom-scented flowers in late spring and early summer.
Striking aroid with dark green leaves and white pinstripes, compact growth habit, variegation can revert to solid green.
Upright, non-vining philodendron with glossy, broad leaves; compact and bushy growth habit.
Rare climbing Philodendron hybrid with ghostly white juvenile leaves that mature to green. Multi-lobed leaves on distinctive red petioles.
Large, highly variegated Philodendron with cream/white and green leaves; statement plant.
Upright Philodendron with new orange leaves that age to green; compact, self-heading habit.
Stunning hybrid philodendron with large, deeply lobed leaves that emerge in brilliant red, orange, and pink tones before maturing to dark green. Highly sought-after collector aroid.
Variegated Philodendron with cream, yellow, orange, and green in leaves; climbing habit.

Also known as: White Knight, White Wizard. Striking white-and-green variegated climbing Philodendrons. White Knight has purple/burgundy stems; White Wizard has pure green stems. Both produce large, dramatically variegated leaves.
Variegated self-heading philodendron with white splashes on green leaves. Slower growing than White Knight, with a more compact habit and brighter white variegation.
Climbing aroid with olive-green, heart-shaped leaves splashed with broad silver patches between the veins.
Fast-growing, easy-care philodendron with narrow, heart-shaped leaves on long stems. Named after the famous Brazilian landscape architect Roberto Burle Marx.
Also known as: PPP. Rare aroid with dark green and pink variegated leaves, requires bright light to maintain variegation, can revert to solid green.
Terrestrial creeping Philodendron with large, velvety heart-shaped leaves featuring prominent white veining. A collector's favorite aroid.
Also known as: Silver sword. Climbing philodendron with elongated, silvery-green leaves.
Also known as: Lemon-lime philodendron. Variegated heart-leaf philodendron with green and yellow-chartreuse leaves, easy-care trailing plant.
Velvety trailing aroid with heart-shaped leaves that shimmer in light, bronze-green with purple undersides.
Also known as: Silver cloud. Crawling Philodendron with silver-marked, heart-shaped leaves. Similar to gloriosum but more compact.
Also known as: Black gold philodendron. Climbing Philodendron with velvety black-green leaves and gold veins; dramatic foliage, needs support.
Crawling philodendron with wavy, elongated leaves and silver veins; grows along the soil surface, not climbing.
Velvety Philodendron with red undersides and prominent veins; requires high humidity.
Also known as: Golden polypody. Epiphytic fern with blue-green fronds and creeping rhizomes; tolerant of lower humidity than most ferns.
Also known as: Garden phlox. Fragrant clusters of flowers in summer in many colors; cottage garden staple. Needs good air circulation to prevent mildew.
Date palm in the Arecaceae family producing sweet drupes, desert-adapted, requires hot dry climate.
Compact date palm with arching fronds; slow-growing. Non-toxic to pets.
Also known as: Red Robin. Evergreen shrub beloved for its brilliant red new growth that matures to glossy dark green. One of the most popular hedging plants in Europe.
Also known as: Golden berry. Fruit in the Solanaceae family with tart-sweet berries enclosed in paper husks, also known as golden berry or ground cherry.
Green husk tomato in the Solanaceae family, essential for salsa verde, tart flavor when ripe.
Small fruit in the Solanaceae family with sweet, tropical-flavored berries in paper husks, related to tomatillo.
Hardy shrub with peeling bark and colorful foliage; white or pink flower clusters.
Evergreen conifer with stiff, sharp needles attached individually to branches. Classic Christmas tree shape. Important timber and paper pulp trees in northern forests.
Also known as: Gray baby tears. Tiny-leaved trailing plant with blue-green foliage; ideal for terrariums or small hanging pots.
Compact tropical foliage plants in the Urticaceae family with round or textured leaves.
